title: Canonical regular quotient completion unit criterion
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Assume countable products of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves are exact. Let $a$ be a global section whose multiplication on $\mathcal O$ is injective. For a K-flat cochain complex $P$ [def-pc-kflat-complex], put $U_n=P\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O/a^n\mathcal O$, restricted to $\mathcal O$, with quotient transitions, and $C_a(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nU_n\to\prod_nU_n)[-1]$. Define $\eta_{a,P}:P\to C_a(P)$ to have product component the quotient maps and zero shifted-product component. Use module-derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Say $N$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete when, for every slice $\mathcal C/V$ and local section $f\in(a)\mathcal O(V)$, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_V}(\mathcal O_V[1/f],N|_V)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], where localization is sheafified sectionwise. Then $C_a(P)$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete. The following are equivalent: $P$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete; $\eta_{a,P}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O)$; there exists a distinguished Roos triangle $P\xrightarrow{(q_n)}\prod_n^D U_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_n^D U_n\to P[1]$ with the prescribed quotient components [def-weil-derived-limit]. These assertions concern the specified zero-component map, not an arbitrarily chosen lift. All tensor products of module sheaves are sheafified tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], applied termwise to complexes when an ordinary tensor is written.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, one regular generator; canonical-unit refinement using the strict Roos comparison and Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 3.4.12.

proof.text: Use the one-generator Koszul tower $Q_n=[\mathcal O\xrightarrow{a^n}\mathcal O]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with transitions $(a,1)$, and put $V_n=P\otimes Q_n$. The degree-zero inclusions define its strict augmentation from $P$. The quotient maps $\epsilon_n:Q_n\to(\mathcal O/a^n\mathcal O)[0]$ commute with transitions: in degree zero both composites are the same quotient map, and in degree minus one both vanish. Their composite with the inclusion of $\mathcal O[0]$ is the quotient projection. Regularity holds for all powers, since $a^n$ is a composite of injective multiplication maps. The regular Koszul reconstruction theorem therefore applies with $t=a$ and the given K-flat $P$: its first assertion gives an augmentation-compatible isomorphism $e:R\lim V_n\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim U_n$. This uses no flatness of the individual terms of $P$.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, one generator, together with the regular-element quotient comparison

proof.text: Write $\Lambda(P)=R\lim V_n$ and $\kappa_P:P\to\Lambda(P)$ for the degree-zero Koszul unit of the ringed-site reflector. Apply the strict Roos comparison to $U_\bullet$. The site is small and its module category has exact countable products, exactly as that comparison requires. It gives $\rho_U:C_a(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim U_n$. Its strict-augmentation normalization says that $\rho_U\eta_{a,P}$ is the derived map induced by the quotient augmentation. Augmentation compatibility of $e$ in Step 1 identifies that same map with $e\kappa_P$. Consequently $\theta=e^{-1}\rho_U:C_a(P)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(P)$ satisfies the actual equality $\theta\eta_{a,P}=\kappa_P$. The zero shifted-product coordinate is essential here: it is exactly the lift to which the cited normalization applies.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, strict Roos resolution comparison and augmentation normalization

proof.text: Apply the ringed-site Koszul completion reflector with the singleton list $(a)$ and $N=P$. Its conclusion is expressed using derived internal Hom on every slice and every local section of the generated ideal, so it is precisely the local condition in the item, with no replacement by completeness merely at global sections. It says that $\Lambda(P)$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete and that $\kappa_P$ is an isomorphism if and only if $P$ is locally derived $(a)$-complete. The isomorphism $\theta$ of Step 2 transfers completeness to $C_a(P)$: restriction and derived internal Hom carry an isomorphism to an isomorphism, so their vanishing conditions agree. The equation $\theta\eta_{a,P}=\kappa_P$ proves that the specified $\eta_{a,P}$ is invertible exactly when $P$ is locally derived complete.

source.place: Tags 099B, lemma-derived-completion, and 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; Tag 0999, definition-derived-complete

proof.text: If $\eta_{a,P}$ is an isomorphism, then $h=\rho_U\eta_{a,P}:P\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim U_n$ is an isomorphism. Take the natural distinguished Roos triangle for $R\lim U_n$ supplied by the ringed strict-tower homotopy-limit theorem, with first map $p$ and connecting map $\delta$. Replace its first vertex by $P$ along $h$, keeping the two product vertices and $1-s$ fixed and replacing the connecting map by $h[1]^{-1}\delta$. The resulting triangle is distinguished by invariance under isomorphism. Its first map is $ph$, whose $n$-th component is $q_n$, since the strict Roos comparison preserves the projections and sends the zero-coordinate quotient lift to the canonical augmentation. Thus this triangle has exactly the prescribed first arrow, not merely some compatible map into the product.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, Roos triangle and its augmentation projections

proof.text: Conversely, assume the stated distinguished triangle with first components $q_n$ exists. Apply the second assertion of regular Koszul reconstruction to $K=P$ and this very triangle. All its hypotheses are available: multiplication by $a$ is injective, $P$ is K-flat, the tower is the quotient tower, and the triangle has the required quotient components. It supplies an isomorphism $\phi:P\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(P)$. The reflector makes $\Lambda(P)$ locally derived complete; therefore $P$ is locally derived complete as well, because slice restriction and derived internal Hom preserve isomorphisms. Step 3 now implies that the specified $\eta_{a,P}$ is an isomorphism. There is no assertion that $\phi$ itself equals the canonical unit: completeness of its source gives invertibility of the canonical unit separately. Together with Steps 3 and 4 this proves all three equivalences.

One commit; the statement is unchanged; no new nodes; not on the dropped list; no re-split note; still unsplit in live and side-live, and the six cited statements match live. Step 1 uses the regular Koszul reconstruction with t=a and K-flat P, and its hypotheses hold. Step 2: the last paragraph of the strict Roos comparison (exact countable products, small site) shows that the zero-shifted-component quotient map eta corresponds to the canonical augmentation. Step 1's augmentation compatibility then gives theta∘eta = kappa (the reflector unit). Since a is regular, (a)O(V)=a·O(V), so the item's completeness condition is literally the reflector's for J=(a). Step 3: the reflector gives completeness of Lambda(P) and of C_a(P), and kappa iso iff P complete, hence eta iso iff P complete. Step 4: transport the homotopy-limit Roos triangle along h=rho∘eta (TR1); its components are q_n because rho commutes with the projections. Advisory: that node's statement does not spell out p's components; I accept the standard meaning. Step 5: the second paragraph of Koszul reconstruction gives P ≅ Lambda(P), so P is complete and eta is an isomorphism by Step 3, with no claim that phi equals kappa. The parent lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison uses exactly the proved directions. Sources: I read Stacks 0A0E lemma-derived-completion-koszul, and 0941 is mapped correctly. Edge cases checked: a a unit, O=0, and O=Z, a=p, P=Z. No cycle in the 646-node dependency closure. No duplicate: the pbc actual-completed reconstruction node needs an adic datum. Accepted tool uses: Koszul reconstruction, the ringed Koszul reflector and the strict-tower homotopy limit, all generic; the unit sk-def-sf-operations has no proof route of its own. No fixes.
